claims.text: The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy is a homogeneous single-phase BCC solid solution.
The WTaTiVZr alloy experiences severe lattice distortion because its constituent elements have different atomic radii.
Lattice distortion in WTaTiVZr modifies the dislocation core structure.
Edge dislocations, rather than screw dislocations, are preferentially activated in WTaTiVZr.
The activated edge dislocations in WTaTiVZr form wavy dislocation lines.
Lattice distortion forces edge dislocations to deviate from their neutral planes.
Wavy edge dislocations are activated more uniformly during high-temperature plastic deformation.
Pure tungsten deforms primarily through temperature-activated screw dislocations under the proposed conditions.
Screw-dislocation-mediated deformation in pure tungsten promotes localized shear and brittleness.
More uniform dislocation activation in WTaTiVZr improves the uniformity of high-temperature plastic deformation.
At 700–900°C under identical mechanical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
At 700–900°C under identical mechanical loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater toughness than pure tungsten.
Dislocation characterization will reveal a higher prevalence of wavy edge dislocations in WTaTiVZr than in pure tungsten.
The comparison will use WTaTiVZr and pure-tungsten specimens with similar grain sizes and controlled processing histories.
Both materials will be mechanically tested at 700–900°C under identical strain rates while their dislocation structures and phases are characterized.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to conditions where WTaTiVZr remains single-phase BCC without significant secondary-phase formation.
The deformation behavior may differ at lower temperatures or under different loading regimes.
Failure to observe enhanced plastic strain or toughness, or failure to observe the predicted prevalence of wavy edge dislocations, would falsify the hypothesis.
